crisis.label: High
crisis.detail: Aug 30: Iran and Oman agreed each side's share of Strait of Hormuz waters and corridor revenues, converting the temporary navigation-corridor framework into a revenue-sharing arrangement (Al Jazeera, Aug 27); Qatar's PM joined mediation efforts in Tehran the same day. Iran's reopening conditions - lifting the naval blockade, unfreezing assets, and removing oil sanctions - remain unmet. Brent is $88.10 (-0.47%, Yahoo Finance, Aug 28) and TTF is 66.98 EUR/MWh (-1.89%, Yahoo Finance, Aug 28). Crisis level remains 4 (High); base 10%, stress 60%, tail 30%.

todaysEvents.delta: Iran's IRGC said Tehran and Muscat agreed each country's share of Strait waters and corridor revenues, converting the temporary framework into a revenue-sharing deal, while Iran kept its blockade-lift and sanctions demands (Al Jazeera, Aug 27).

todaysEvents.summary: Qatar PM joins Hormuz mediation push
todaysEvents.delta: Qatar's PM Sheikh Mohammed met Iranian officials in Tehran to review de-escalation efforts, following Pakistan's Aug 24 and Oman's Aug 25 visits; Iran still opposes the southern Oman-route channel (Al Jazeera, Aug 27).
Brent is $88.14, down 0.43%, WTI is $83.02, down 0.61%, and TTF is 68.80 EUR/MWh, up 0.7%, as corridor diplomacy met continued LNG supply risk (Trading Economics/Yahoo Finance, Aug 27-28).

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Iran and Oman advance a temporary corridor and mine-clearance framework; a signed, monitored reopening restores traffic and lowers Brent toward $75-85, while Qatar's force majeure keeps LNG availability constrained.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: The corridor remains provisional and traffic stays selective under Iranian fees, sanctions pressure and residual mine and attack risk; Brent holds $78-95 and JKM stays elevated while Qatar's force majeure runs through mid-September.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: A failed framework, further tanker attack or sanctions retaliation could close the southern lane again and spill into Bab el-Mandeb; Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu.
